messages:
mike_marketing: quick post-experiment update — we ran the claim quota burst test against HS on the staging stream at 09:00 PT. results inside.

jess_dev: :eyes: saw some anomalous drop in successful claims around 09:02, sending logs now.

opsbot: deploy-status: canary -> 4912345678-claim-burst (3/3 hosts) succeeded

mike_marketing: tl;dr: lead arrival spike + quota-burst attempted to speed claims by 4x. success rate fell from 98% -> 76% during peak 09:01–09:05. average claim latency doubled.

sanah_salesops: ouch. any idea why latency spiked? HS webhook queueing? sticky-owner checks?

rahul_eng: digging — two things: HubSpot webhooks were fine, but our claim worker pool hit request bursts and exhausted token buckets. also observed claim ack timeouts due to heartbeat debounce at 30s.

jess_dev: logs: `claim_worker.overflow` and `rr_assign_retry` spikes. example: ``ERROR claim_worker: rate limit exceeded for org_id=acme-corp``

mike_marketing: thanks — can you confirm if this is capacity misconfig or a logic bug that amplifies bursts?

rahul_eng: it's config + routing policy. round-robin assignment retries currently back off with full jitter up to 60s; when burst happens retries queue and cause thundering herd on release. essentially retry storms.

sanah_salesops: thats the product pain customers felt yesterday — some leads stayed unassigned for ~5m. we got two support tickets.

mike_marketing: note: this experiment was intentional load to reproduce that behavior. good we caught it in staging but need a patch plan before next prod push.

jess_dev: proposal: 1) reduce heartbeat debounce from 30s -> 8s in staging for canary; 2) cap per-org claim QPS to 20 (was unlimited); 3) introduce progressive retry with linear backoff and jitter cap 5s.

rahul_eng: agree. also add a soft-queue that drains at steady rate (token-bucket) to avoid instant fanout when many retries happen.

sanah_salesops: for HS/SF mapping: if enrichment lag > 45s, mark lead as pending and surface to SDR queue instead of retrying claims endlessly. that should reduce stuck leads.

mike_marketing: ok action items: 
- rahul_eng: implement retry cap + soft-queue (owner: @rahul_eng, due: 2026-04-02)
- jess_dev: spike heartbeat debounce change and config toggle (owner: @jess_dev, due: 2026-03-30)
- sanah_salesops: craft customer comms/playbook for short outages (owner: @sanah_salesops, due: 2026-04-03)

rahul_eng: patch plan: feature flag gates, release to staging canary, smoke test with 2x burst, monitor metrics: claim_success_rate, claim_latency_p90, pending_leads_count. revert flag if claim_success < 95%.

opsbot: perf-alert rule created: `claim_success_rate < 95% for 2m` -> paging to eng-oncall

jess_dev: quick note on metrics: observed p95 latency 1.8s -> 4.5s in burst. token consumption spikes correspond 1:1 with claim failures.

mike_marketing: ok let's not over-index on perfect latency for now — goal is no more >2m unassigned lead windows. if staging checks pass, we'll roll to a small prod canary (5% routing) and monitor for 48h.

sanah_salesops: can we add a short-term fallback in HubSpot mapping: if owner not assigned after 90s, route to global overflow pool with email notify? customers want quick contact.

rahul_eng: yes, implement fallback route toggle behind same flag. it's cheap and reduces customer-visible impact.

mike_marketing: final: schedule follow-up sync Wed 11:00 PT. expected quick wins: retry cap + heartbeat tuning + overflow fallback. if all green, update handoff SLA docs and playbook.

jess_dev: noted. I'll open PRs and link here. :thumbsup:

sanah_salesops: I'll prepare canned comms and SDR playbook changes after we see canary metrics.

mike_marketing: thanks team — great repro and clear next steps.
